blueprint_concepts: Distance formula, Section formula, harmonic conjugate
Four points(Centroid, Incenter, circumcenter, orthocenter) of a triangle

concept_use.Distance formula, Section formula, harmo: D and E divide AB internally and externally in the ratio 2:1 (section formula, harmonic conjugates): D = (6,0), E = (18,0).
concept_use.Four points(Centroid, Incenter, circumce: The centroid G = (A+B+C)/3 moves on a circle of radius 2 centred at (7,0).
concept_use.Area of triangle: The area of triangle DEG is (1/2)(DE)(height of G above AB) = 12|sin theta|, maximised to 12.
concept_use.Locus based questions: The locus of C (CA = 2CB) is the circle on DE as diameter, and the locus of G is found from it.

english: Let $A(0,0)$ and $B(9,0)$. A point $C$, not on the $x$-axis, moves in such a way that $CA=2\,CB$. The bisectors of the interior and the exterior angles of triangle $ABC$ at $C$ meet the line $AB$ at $D$ and $E$ respectively, and $G$ is the centroid of triangle $ABC$. Then the maximum value of the area of triangle $DEG$ is ______.
hindi: माना $A(0,0)$ तथा $B(9,0)$ है। एक बिन्दु $C$, जो $x$-अक्ष पर नहीं है, इस प्रकार गति करता है कि $CA=2\,CB$ है। त्रिभुज $ABC$ के शीर्ष $C$ पर अन्तः कोण तथा बाह्य कोण के समद्विभाजक रेखा $AB$ से क्रमशः $D$ तथा $E$ पर मिलते हैं, तथा $G$ त्रिभुज $ABC$ का केन्द्रक है। तब त्रिभुज $DEG$ के क्षेत्रफल का अधिकतम मान ______ है।
solution: Bisector theorem: $D$ and $E$ divide $AB$ internally and externally in $CA:CB=2:1$, so they are fixed harmonic conjugates: $D=(6,0)$, $E=(18,0)$
Since $\angle DCE=90^\circ$, $C$ lies on the circle on $DE$ as diameter: centre $(12,0)$, radius $6$ (the locus of $CA=2CB$)
$D,E$ are on the $x$-axis with $DE=12$, so area $DEG=\dfrac12\cdot12\cdot|2\sin\theta|\le12$
Maximum at $C=(12,\pm6)$, which is not on the $x$-axis
solution_full: By the interior and exterior angle-bisector theorems, $D$ divides $AB$ internally and $E$ divides $AB$ externally in the ratio $CA:CB=2:1$. So $D$ and $E$ are harmonic conjugates with respect to $A,B$, and they do not depend on the position of $C$.
The two bisectors at $C$ are perpendicular, so $\angle DCE=90^\circ$ and $C$ lies on the circle with diameter $DE$: centre $(12,0)$, radius $6$.

Write $C=(12+6\cos\theta,\,6\sin\theta)$, $\sin\theta\neq0$. The centroid is $G=\left(\dfrac{0+9+12+6\cos\theta}{3},\dfrac{6\sin\theta}{3}\right)=(7+2\cos\theta,\,2\sin\theta)$, so $G$ moves on a circle of radius $2$ centred at $(7,0)$.
$D$ and $E$ lie on the $x$-axis with $DE=12$, so the area of triangle $DEG$ is $\dfrac12\cdot12\cdot|2\sin\theta|=12|\sin\theta|$.
The maximum is $12$, attained for $\theta=\pm\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, i.e. $C=(12,\pm6)$, which is allowed.
originality_note: New: the feet of the two bisectors at the moving vertex are fixed harmonic conjugates (way 4: a hidden invariant), the locus of C is the circle on DE, and the centroid traces a scaled circle, so the area of DEG is maximised without calculus. Closest known: 'locus of C with CA = k CB is a circle' (Apollonius). Different because: the question is about the triangle formed by the bisector feet and the centroid, which is clean only after noticing D and E are fixed.
stem_review: Read as a student: every point, line, curve and symbol is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath (and a numerical brute-force check), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Stated that C is not on the x-axis so the triangle exists; the maximum is attained at C = (12, 6), which is allowed. Changed: No change.
key_step: Seeing that D and E are fixed (harmonic division in the ratio 2:1) and that the centroid traces a circle of radius 2.
justification: Two linked ideas (bisector theorem giving fixed harmonic points, locus scaled to the centroid) with an area maximum; numerical but short once seen. Comparable to the locus-and-area demand of 2026-P1-Q2 (L2) plus a non-obvious invariant, so L3.
